note: Resume-detection eval: read-only, no side effects. Each fixture is a project at a different pipeline state; the skill's Step 1 must pick the correct entry stage and, when the state is ambiguous, confirm rather than guess. Only the statically representable states are committed here. The later transitions (installed->verify, verified->document) depend on a fully resolved dependency tree and a runtime pass, which are not capturable as a small static fixture; the orchestrator re-verifies for those rather than trusting a stale signal. Fixture E is the exception that carries a resolved lock and a test file, and its prompt states the checks pass, because what it exercises is the old-layout branch rather than verify detection.

evals.name: empty-project
evals.prompt: Set up the whole tech stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR. (Dry run: report which stage you would START at and why; do not run any stage, install, or command.)
evals.expected_output: ENTRY STAGE: identify-stack-slots. No .claude/stack-it/ artifacts at all (only IDEA.md), so it starts at the top of the pipeline. Unambiguous.

evals.name: slots-only
evals.prompt: Set up the whole tech stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR. (Dry run: report which stage you would START at and why; do not run any stage, install, or command.)
evals.expected_output: ENTRY STAGE: decide-stack. .claude/stack-it/slots.yaml exists and validates, but there is no stack.yaml, so the slots are identified but tools aren't decided. Unambiguous.

evals.name: locked-not-installed
evals.prompt: Set up the whole tech stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR. (Dry run: report which stage you would START at and why; do not run any stage, install, or command.)
evals.expected_output: ENTRY STAGE: install-stack. A complete .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml exists but nothing is installed (no manifests, no node_modules), so the tools are decided but not installed. Should NOT restart at identify/decide even though slots.yaml is absent, since the downstream artifact already exists. Unambiguous.

evals.name: ambiguous-partial-install
evals.prompt: Set up the whole tech stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR. (Dry run: report which stage you would START at and why; do not run any stage, install, or command.)
evals.expected_output: The signature fail-safe (SKILL.md Step 1): stack.yaml exists, a package.json is present, and a node_modules/ directory exists but resolves nothing (only an empty .package-lock.json), a false 'installed' signal. The skill must NOT trust the bare node_modules and skip ahead; it should treat the state as ambiguous and CONFIRM the entry stage with the user before proceeding (most likely install-stack, since nothing is actually resolved).

evals.name: verified-old-layout
evals.prompt: Set up the whole tech stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR. Assume the build, lint, tests, and dev server all pass. (Dry run: report which stage you would START at and why; do not run any stage, install, or command.)
evals.expected_output: ENTRY STAGE: document-stack. Everything is installed (package.json plus a node_modules/.package-lock.json that resolves react, vite, vitest, eslint and the rest) and there is a verification slice (src/ContactForm.test.tsx), so the pipeline is verified. It is also documented, but on the OLD layout: CLAUDE.md carries a <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block, there is no docs/stack.md, no AGENTS.md, and stack.yaml has no format key. That is format 1, which is not finished work, so the skill must NOT report 'all done'. It routes to document-stack, which calls migrate to restructure before refreshing. The expected note: read CLAUDE.md from disk to see the marker, since Claude Code strips HTML comments from loaded context.
